description: Our team, InterstellarX, is participating in the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge under the Dancing with the SARs challenge. Our core motive is to build an automated pipeline using NISAR radar data to process multi-temporal Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery and track surface changes over time. By combining geospatial tools with machine learning, we aim to turn complex radar data into clear, actionable insights for environmental monitoring.
summary:
Team InterstellarX developed an end-to-end local geospatial processing pipeline and interactive web dashboard to monitor and quantify tropical wetland inundation across the Amazon Basin (Manaus region). Utilizing next-generation NISAR L-band HHHH backscatter data from L2 GCOV products, our solution directly addresses the "Dancing with the SARs" challenge by capturing multi-temporal hydrological shifts between peak flood conditions (June 2026) and dry baselines (November 2026). 

To overcome high-resolution big-data processing bottlenecks, we implemented memory-efficient h5py array slicing and a robust logarithmic change-detection algorithm, ln(Wet/Dry), isolating specular water reflection from vegetation canopy scattering. These insights are integrated into a production-grade Streamlit web application featuring real-time threshold control sliders, dynamic flood extent percentage calculations, and statistical backscatter distribution histograms. By transforming complex orbital radar observations into actionable, interactive intelligence, this tool provides researchers and disaster response teams with rapid, transparent, and reproducible flood-monitoring capabilities.
details:
Team InterstellarX presents an end-to-end local remote sensing workflow and interactive dashboard designed to monitor tropical wetland inundation and flood dynamics in the Amazon Basin (Manaus region) using next-generation NISAR L-band data.

Key Technical Highlights:

1. High-Performance HDF5 Processing: Bypassed GDAL virtual path limitations by utilizing direct, memory-efficient `h5py` slicing to extract dual-polarized HHHH radar backscatter arrays and spatial coordinates from multi-gigabyte NISAR L2 GCOV `.h5` containers.

2. Multi-Temporal Change Detection: Implemented a robust logarithmic change-detection algorithm [ln(Wet / Dry)] to isolate specular water reflection from vegetation canopy scattering between peak flood (June 23, 2026) and dry baseline (November 2, 2026) passes.

3. Interactive Web Dashboard: Developed a production-grade Streamlit application featuring real-time threshold sliders, dynamic flood extent percentage calculations, statistical backscatter distribution histograms, and GeoTIFF/matrix export triggers.
